system_overview: This specification models an intentionally erroneous variant of the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment Protocol (ACP-NB). The mistake is that a participant delivers a broadcast decision locally (decides) BEFORE forwarding it to all other participants, violating the correct protocol's requirement to forward first and decide only after forwarding is complete. This subtle ordering bug causes the fundamental consistency property (AC1) to fail: TLC can find executions where one participant commits while another aborts.
actors_and_components: The same actors as the correct ACP-NB: a set of participants and a single coordinator. The coordinator collects votes and broadcasts a decision. Participants vote and attempt to relay decisions to each other, but with a flawed broadcast order.
state_variables: Same as the correct ACP-NB: each participant has a vote, alive flag, decision, faulty flag, vote-sent flag, and a forwarding table mapping each participant to a forwarding status (not-sent, commit, or abort). The coordinator has request tracking, vote tracking, broadcast tracking, decision, alive flag, and faulty flag.
initial_state: Same as the correct ACP-NB: all participants start alive, non-faulty, undecided, with a nondeterministic yes/no vote and all forwarding entries set to not-sent. The coordinator starts alive, non-faulty, undecided, with no requests or votes processed.
actions: Coordinator actions are identical to the correct protocol. The participant actions include the base ACP-SB actions (send vote, abort on vote, abort on timeout for request, decide from coordinator broadcast). The key difference from the correct ACP-NB is: (1) Forward (erroneous): a participant forwards based on its DECISION rather than its pre-decision -- meaning it has already decided before forwarding. It forwards its decided value to other participants. (2) Decide on forward (erroneous): when a participant receives a forwarded decision from another participant, it immediately decides (rather than pre-deciding and forwarding first). (3) Abort on timeout: same conditions as the correct variant. The critical bug is that participants decide immediately upon receiving a decision (either from the coordinator or from another participant's forward), and only then forward to others. If a participant decides and then crashes before forwarding, other participants may time out and abort, leading to inconsistency.
safety_properties: This specification is designed to VIOLATE the consistency property AC1: it is possible for one participant to commit while another aborts. TLC detects this violation and produces a counterexample trace.
model_bounds: The participant set is instantiated with 2 model values for checking. TLC finds the AC1 violation with this small configuration.
additional_assumptions: This module extends the base ACP-SB specification and reuses its coordinator logic. Weak fairness is assumed on participant and coordinator progress actions. The specification is intentionally incorrect and serves as a pedagogical example showing how TLC can catch subtle distributed protocol bugs.
